\subsection*{Class NP --- Poly Time Block Majority: Results}

\begin{definition}[Majority computation step]
\lean{Complexity.majStep}
\label{Complexity.majStep}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BlockLoop.step, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Complexity.sliceDropAt, Complexity.sliceTakeAt, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.pairEncode}
Given a language $V$ of Boolean lists and natural numbers $a$ and $k$, define a state
update on Boolean lists using the block-loop step operation. Its update decodes the
state as a pair, tests whether the specified length-$k$ slice of the second component
belongs to $V$, and encodes the corresponding updated nested pair together with the
remaining slice.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Majority computation emission]
\lean{Complexity.majEmit}
\label{Complexity.majEmit}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BlockLoop.emit, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD}
For a Boolean list $s$, emit the negation of the test that the length of the first list
in the specified nested pair decoding of $s$ is at most the length of the second list in
that decoding.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Majority computation initialization]
\lean{Complexity.majInit}
\label{Complexity.majInit}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Turing.pairEncode}
Given natural numbers $a'$ and $k'$ and a Boolean list $z$, encode a state whose first
component is the singleton list containing true. Its second component encodes a list of
$a' (m+1)^{k'}$ true values, followed by empty-list components and the two lists
obtained by decoding $z$ as a pair, where $m$ is the length of the first decoded list.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Length bound for an encoded vote]
\lean{Complexity.length_majVote_le}
\label{Complexity.length_majVote_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.length_pair_components_le, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Turing.length_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
For every bit $b$ and bit string $a$, encode the pair whose first component is the total
first projection of $a$ with an initial $1$ prepended and whose second component is the
total second projection of $a$ with an initial $1$ prepended, if $b=1$; if $b=0$,
prepend the initial $1$ only to the second component. In either case, the resulting
encoded string has length at most $|a|+4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Output of the majority loop]
\lean{Complexity.majLoop_output}
\label{Complexity.majLoop_output}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BlockLoop.loop_output, Complexity.BlockLoop.lt_polyBudget_of_le, Complexity.BlockLoop.sliceDropAt_pairEncode_drop, Complexity.BlockLoop.sliceTakeAt_pairEncode_drop, Complexity.blockAt, Complexity.majEmit, Complexity.majInit, Complexity.majStep, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairFstD_pairEncode, Complexity.pairSndD, Complexity.pairSndD_pairEncode, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.length_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{6}
Let $V$ be a language of bit strings, let $a,k,a',k'$ be natural numbers, and let $z$ be
a bit string. Put $N=a'(|\pi_1(z)|+1)^{k'}$, and for each $j<N$ let $B_j$ be the
length-$a(|\pi_1(z)|+1)^k$ block of $\pi_2(z)$ beginning at position $j
a(|\pi_1(z)|+1)^k$. Iterating the prescribed block-loop step from its prescribed
initialization and concatenating the emissions for $N+1$ iterations yields the one-bit
list whose bit is true exactly when $N<2\,|\{j<N: \langle\pi_1(z),B_j\rangle\in V\}|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-Time Block Majority Test]
\lean{Complexity.polyTimeComputable_blockMajorityTest}
\label{Complexity.polyTimeComputable_blockMajorityTest}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BlockLoop.polyTimeComputable_countdown, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.comp, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode, Complexity.blockAt, Complexity.length_majVote_le, Complexity.length_pair_components_le, Complexity.length_sliceDropAt_le, Complexity.majEmit, Complexity.majLoop_output, Complexity.majStep, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_const, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_ite, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_lenLe, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_not, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairFstD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairSndD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_prepend, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_sliceDropAt, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_sliceTakeAt, Complexity.sliceTakeAt, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.length_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Let $V$ be a language of finite bit strings whose Boolean membership indicator, output
as a one-bit word, is polynomial-time computable. For any $a,k,a',k'\in\mathbb{N}$, the
following function is polynomial-time computable: on input $z$, let $x$ be the first
component obtained by parsing $z$ as a pair (using the empty word if parsing fails), and
test the first $N=a'(|x|+1)^{k'}$ blocks of length $a(|x|+1)^k$ in the parsed second
component, treating an unavailable block as the empty word. The output is true exactly
when strictly more than half of these $N$ blocks, paired with $x$, belong to $V$.
\end{theorem}
